description: Assertions for tools/notebook-eval.js. Two-sided, like the prose corpus: must_fire proves the auditor still catches a defect, must_not_fire proves it has not become so permissive that it waves everything through. must_resolve is the third axis this tool needs — proof it can still SEE a reference, since its historical failure was parsing nothing and reporting a clean run.

cases.name: current-notation
cases.why: Regime tags, rank-type tags, and parallel ID namespaces (K-bbox-3, K-leak-7a, K27.3) are what consumers actually write. Until 2026-08-31 the pattern was K\d+ anchored at '[NB', so all of these were skipped in silence and the audit reported clean.

cases.name: unparseable-aggregate
cases.why: An aggregate whose headings are the wrong level parses to zero claims. That must be an error, not a run in which every reference is silently unvalidated.

cases.name: claims-but-no-refs
cases.why: A populated aggregate and zero parsed references means the reference pattern failed, not that the prose is clean. This is the exact shape of the 2026-04-to-08 silent failure.

cases.name: stale-ref-still-caught
cases.why: Guards the other direction: widening the K-ID grammar must not make the matcher so permissive that an unresolvable claim passes.

cases.name: notebook-block-defects
cases.why: A Key Claims block holding a stdout fragment renders as present and parses to zero rows; it used to display a checkmark. Two notebook files under one label make every reference to that label ambiguous and merge their claims in the aggregate.
